Read docs/TASK_contour_engine.md FIRST (sections 2.1, 2.2, 2.3 -- the exact names and shapes; do not guess a field name, every one is there or in resources/contour-engine.openapi.json, both in your context), then docs/EXAMPLES.md (the acceptance examples; your tests cite example numbers). You write the pure schema layer of a Contour engine: parsing of the two request shapes of the OpenAPI, and derivation of relationship edges from a record body. No I/O, no sqlite, no HTTP; stdlib only; Python 3.9 syntax (typing.List/Dict/Optional/Tuple, no `match`, no `X | Y`).

Write TWO new files.

1. `contour_engine/schema.py` -- module-level names, exactly these:

    ELEMENT_TYPES = ("SYSTEM", "COMPONENT", "FUNCTION", "INTERFACE", "EVENT", "DATA_OBJECT", "ACTOR")
    OWNED_TYPES = frozenset({"FUNCTION", "INTERFACE", "EVENT", "DATA_OBJECT"})
    VERBS = ("groups", "performs", "exposes", "uses", "calls", "produces", "consumes", "reads", "modifies", "owns", "references", "depends-on")
    STEP_VERBS = ("calls", "reads", "modifies", "produces", "uses")
    FIELD_VERBS = {"groups": "groups", "performs": "performs", "owns": "owns", "produces": "produces", "references": "references", "consumes": "consumes", "dependsOn": "depends-on", "exposes": "exposes", "uses": "uses"}
    RECORD_FIELDS = {"SYSTEM": ("groups",), "COMPONENT": ("performs", "owns", "produces", "references", "consumes", "dependsOn"), "FUNCTION": ("behavior", "steps"), "INTERFACE": ("schema", "exposes"), "DATA_OBJECT": ("schema",), "EVENT": ("schema",), "ACTOR": ("uses",)}
    IRREGULAR_PAST = frozenset({...})   # the list of EXAMPLES example 8, lower-cased
    def is_past_tense(name) -> bool
    def parse_element_request(payload) -> Tuple[Optional[dict], List[dict]]
    def parse_definition_request(payload) -> Tuple[Optional[dict], List[dict]]
    def declared_edges(element_type, record) -> List[Tuple[str, str, str]]

A violation is `{"ref": str, "message": str}` (TASK 2.2). `parse_element_request(payload)`: payload is the decoded JSON of an OpenAPI `ElementRequest`. Return `(request, violations)`; `request` is None when violations is non-empty. Checks, each producing a violation with `ref` = the JSON path of the offending field (`"name"`, `"elementType"`, `"record.description"`, `"record.steps[2]"`, `"record.requirements"`, ...): payload is an object; `name` is a non-empty string; `elementType` is in ELEMENT_TYPES (example 18); `id`, `modelId`, `systemId`, `componentId` when present are non-empty strings (uuid format is NOT enforced here); `record` is an object with a non-empty string `description` (example 17); `record.requirements` / `record.guardrails` when present are NameLists (non-empty list of unique non-empty strings; a duplicate or an empty string or an empty list is a violation on that field); type-specific fields per RECORD_FIELDS: NameList fields as above, `behavior` a non-empty string when present, `schema` a non-empty string or a non-empty object, `steps` a non-empty list of single-key objects whose key is in STEP_VERBS and whose value is a non-empty string (violation ref `record.steps[i]`); an EVENT whose name fails `is_past_tense` -> violation ref `"name"`, message containing `past tense` (example 8). Collect ALL violations, never stop at the first (example 10). The returned `request` is a plain dict with keys `id` (None when absent), `modelId`, `name`, `elementType`, `systemId`, `componentId`, `record` (the record dict as given).

`parse_definition_request(payload)`: `DefinitionRequest {name, description}`, both non-blank strings after `.strip()` (example 27); returns `({"name", "description"}, [])` or `(None, violations)`.

`is_past_tense(name)`: take the last whitespace-separated word, lower-case, strip punctuation; True when it ends with `ed` or is in IRREGULAR_PAST; False for empty. Exactly the rule of EXAMPLES example 8 -- copy the irregular list from there.

`declared_edges(element_type, record)`: the relationship edges a record declares, in field order of RECORD_FIELDS then list order, as `(verb, target_name, ref)` where ref is the JSON path (`record.groups[0]`, `record.steps[1].calls`); for FUNCTION only `steps` produce edges (each step `{verb: name}` -> `(verb, name, ref)`); `behavior`, `schema`, `description`, `requirements`, `guardrails` produce none. Unknown fields are ignored. This function is the ONLY place that knows which record field is which edge (TASK 2.1 table) -- say so in the docstring.

Module docstring: what the module does NOT do (no persistence, no invariants that need stored state -- ownership and target existence are the engine's job; no HTTP). Comments explain WHY (why validation collects all violations, why the past-tense rule is a heuristic and marked as an interpretation).

2. `tests/test_schema.py` -- unittest, `msg=` on every assertion, each test method's docstring names the EXAMPLES number(s) it covers. Cover: a valid SYSTEM request parses with `id` None; missing name / bad elementType / missing description each yield exactly the documented ref (18, 17); two problems at once -> two violations (10); NameList with a duplicate and with an empty string -> violation; steps with an unknown verb and with a two-key object -> violation ref `record.steps[i]`; `is_past_tense`: `Element Stored` True, `Element Store` False, `Order Sent` True, `Data Read` False, `` False; EVENT `Element Store` -> violation on `name` mentioning past tense (8); `declared_edges` for each of the seven types on a record built from the examples in TASK 2.1 (e.g. COMPONENT with performs/owns/produces/references/consumes/dependsOn -> verbs in that order with `depends-on` spelled with a hyphen; FUNCTION with three steps -> three edges in step order with refs `record.steps[0].calls` etc.; INTERFACE exposes; ACTOR uses; SYSTEM groups; DATA_OBJECT and EVENT -> []); `parse_definition_request` accepts a good body and rejects blank name / blank description / non-object.

extra_cards.instruction:
Read docs/TASK_contour_engine.md FIRST (2.1 the Data Objects and their fields, 2.2, 2.3 the exact names of this module) and docs/EXAMPLES.md (examples 15, 22, 26, 41 and the search examples 33-38, 42 are yours at the persistence level). You write the persistence layer of a Contour engine on sqlite3 (stdlib) with FTS5. No validation of Contour invariants here (the engine does that), no HTTP, no JSON parsing of requests. Python 3.9 syntax, stdlib only.

Write TWO new files.

1. `contour_engine/store.py` -- `class Store` with `__init__(self, path=":memory:")`, `connect()` (idempotent; creates schema if absent), `close()`, `transaction()` (a context manager: BEGIN on enter, COMMIT on normal exit, ROLLBACK on exception and re-raise -- nested use must not open a second transaction; use a depth counter), and `self.conn` (the sqlite3 connection, `row_factory = sqlite3.Row`). Schema (create with `IF NOT EXISTS`):

- `elements(id TEXT PRIMARY KEY, model_id TEXT NOT NULL, name TEXT NOT NULL, element_type TEXT NOT NULL, system_id TEXT, component_id TEXT, version INTEGER NOT NULL, created_at TEXT NOT NULL, updated_at TEXT NOT NULL)` with indexes on `(model_id, name)` and `(model_id, element_type)`;
- `records(element_id TEXT PRIMARY KEY REFERENCES elements(id), body TEXT NOT NULL)` -- body is the record JSON text;
- `relationships(id TEXT PRIMARY KEY, model_id TEXT NOT NULL, from_element_id TEXT NOT NULL, to_element_id TEXT NOT NULL, verb TEXT NOT NULL)` with indexes on `from_element_id` and on `to_element_id`;
- `requirements(name TEXT PRIMARY KEY, description TEXT NOT NULL, version INTEGER NOT NULL, created_at TEXT NOT NULL, updated_at TEXT NOT NULL)` and `guardrails(...)` identical;
- FTS5 virtual tables `elements_fts(element_id UNINDEXED, name, body)`, `requirements_fts(name, description)`, `guardrails_fts(name, description)` kept in sync by the write primitives (delete old row + insert; do not use external-content tables, keep it simple and correct). Index names must contain the column names so a test can find them in `sqlite_master` (example 41).

Primitives (all take/return plain dicts with the camelCase keys of the OpenAPI views -- `id, modelId, name, elementType, systemId, componentId, version, createdAt, updatedAt, record` -- converting from the snake_case columns; timestamps are ISO-8601 UTC strings with a trailing `Z`):
- `upsert_element(request) -> dict`: request is the parsed ElementRequest dict (keys id, modelId, name, elementType, systemId, componentId, record); when `id` is None generate `str(uuid.uuid4())`; insert with version 1, or update name/type/owners/record and set `version = version + 1`, `updated_at = now`; write the record body as `json.dumps(record, sort_keys=True)`; refresh the FTS row with `name` and a body text made of the record's description, behavior and schema (schema stringified) joined by spaces; return the view. Must be called inside `transaction()` by the caller OR open its own -- implement: if no transaction is active, wrap itself in one.
- `get_element(element_id) -> Optional[dict]` (view with `record` decoded from JSON).
- `delete_element(element_id) -> int`: deletes relationships where the id is either endpoint, the record, the FTS row, the element; returns 1 if the element existed else 0.
- `replace_outgoing(element_id, model_id, edges) -> None`: `edges` is a list of `(verb, to_element_id)`; delete all relationships with `from_element_id == element_id`, insert the new ones with `str(uuid.uuid4())` ids, in order.
- `list_relationships(element_id) -> List[dict]` with keys `id, modelId, fromElementId, toElementId, verb` for rows where the id is either endpoint.
- `list_model(model_id) -> Tuple[List[dict], List[dict]]`: all element views (without record decoding cost is fine, include record) and all relationships of the model.
- `count(table) -> int`.
- `find_by_name(model_id, name, component_id=None) -> List[dict]`: elements of the model with that exact name; when `component_id` is given restrict to `component_id == that OR id == that` (the component itself may be the target, e.g. `dependsOn`).
- `search_elements(q, model_id=None) -> List[dict]`: FTS5 MATCH on `elements_fts` (quote the query as a phrase to be safe against FTS syntax: wrap in double quotes with inner quotes doubled), joined to `elements`, each result `{elementId, modelId, name, elementType, description}` where description is read from the record body; ordered by FTS rank.
- `list_elements(model_id=None, element_type=None, page=0, size=20) -> dict`: a PagedResult `{items, page, size, totalElements, totalPages}` with items as SearchResult dicts ordered by name, `totalPages = ceil(total/size)` (0 when total 0).
- `upsert_definition(kind, name, description) -> dict` (kind in {"requirements", "guardrails"}; insert version 1 or update version+1; refresh FTS; return `{name, description, version, createdAt, updatedAt}`), `get_definition(kind, name)`, `delete_definition(kind, name) -> int`, `search_definitions(kind, q) -> List[dict]` (`{name, description}`), `definition_referenced(kind, name) -> bool`: True when any record body's `requirements` (for kind requirements) or `guardrails` (for kind guardrails) list contains the name -- read the JSON bodies in Python; correctness over speed.

Module docstring names what the store does NOT do (no Contour invariants, no HTTP, no events) and WHY the FTS tables are plain (not external-content): one writer, small data, no drift. Comments say WHY the transaction depth counter exists (the engine wraps several primitives in one all-or-nothing write, examples 11, 15, 22).

2. `tests/test_store.py` -- unittest with `msg=`, docstrings citing EXAMPLES numbers; use `Store(":memory:")`. Cover: after `connect()` `sqlite_master` lists the five tables, the three FTS tables, and indexes whose names mention `from_element_id`, `to_element_id`, `model_id` (41); upsert twice -> version 2 and one row (26 at store level); `transaction()` rolls back everything when the body raises (insert an element then raise; count is 0) and nested `transaction()` does not commit early (15, 22); `delete_element` removes record and relationships on both sides and returns 0 on a missing id (19, 20); `replace_outgoing` replaces (13); `search_elements` finds by name and by description body and returns [] for `zzqx` (34, 35), results have exactly the five SearchResult keys (36); `list_elements` paging math with 25 elements, size 10, page 1 -> 10 items, totalPages 3 (38); `find_by_name` with and without component scoping (14); definitions: upsert/version, search by description word, `definition_referenced` True after an element record lists the name and False otherwise (30); timestamps end with `Z`.

Read docs/TASK_contour_engine.md (2.2 'Mermaid', 2.3 the names of this module) and docs/EXAMPLES.md examples 44, 45, 47, 48. You write a pure Mermaid renderer: lists of dicts in, text out. No I/O, no sqlite, no engine imports. Python 3.9 syntax.

Write TWO new files.

1. `contour_engine/diagram.py` -- module-level names, exactly these: `def node_id(uuid_str) -> str` (a Mermaid-safe identifier: `n_` + the uuid with hyphens removed), `def label(name) -> str` (the name with double quotes replaced by single quotes, wrapped in double quotes so spaces and parentheses are safe: `["Store Element"]`), `def render_model(elements, relationships) -> str`, `def render_element(element, neighbours, relationships) -> str`.

Input shapes: an element dict has at least `id, name, elementType`; a relationship dict has `fromElementId, toElementId, verb`. `render_model`: first line exactly `flowchart LR`; then one node line per element, sorted by (elementType, name) for determinism: `    <node_id>["<name>"]` -- for a COMPONENT or SYSTEM use a `subgraph`? NO: keep it flat, one node per element, but append the type as a suffix inside the label: `["Store Element (FUNCTION)"]`; then one edge line per relationship: `    <from> -->|<verb>| <to>`, with duplicates removed (same from, to, verb) and sorted by (from, verb, to). A relationship whose endpoint is not among the given elements is skipped (the caller may pass a partial set). No trailing spaces, lines joined with `\n`, final newline.

`render_element(element, neighbours, relationships)`: same format, nodes = the element plus the neighbours (deduplicated by id), edges = only those relationships touching the element's id (either side) and whose other end is among the nodes -- the focused diagram of example 47.

Module docstring says what the module does NOT do (no reading, no ordering promise for steps: edges are an unordered summary, so they are sorted for determinism -- cite the record's Render Diagram behavior).

2. `tests/test_diagram.py` -- unittest with `msg=`, docstrings citing 44, 45, 47: build 5 elements and 6 relationships by hand (with one duplicate edge and one edge to an unknown id); assert the header line; one node line per element with the label containing the name and the type; exactly 5 edge lines (duplicate collapsed, unknown-endpoint edge skipped) each containing `-->|verb|`; determinism (two renders equal; shuffled input renders equal); `render_element` on a hub element with two out and one in edges shows exactly 4 nodes and 3 edges and nothing else; `label('a"b')` has no double quote inside; `node_id` starts with `n_` and has no hyphens.
